messages.text: For a Aerospace / Defense use case involving radar, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

The CMX500 is positioned as a callbox that quickly establishes a DUT connection for RF, mobility, application, NTN, WLAN/cellular desense, pre-conformance, and non-signaling R&D verification [1].
Its example use cases include R&D verification of new bands, sensitivity testing, desense testing, 3GPP pre-conformance testing, RF measurements, high-throughput testing, and non-signaling verification [9].
In an A&D context, the supported mission drivers are tactical-edge connectivity, smart jamming/EW, contested spectrum, private 5G, autonomous systems and drones needing low latency, and secure command-and-control networks [10].
The roadmap context also mentions early ISAC deployment for drone detection and perimeter defense, but it does not define a radar test workflow [3].
The CMX500 is also described as a 5G one-box signaling tester that supports early R&D through fading and channel emulation, plus satellite-constellation visualization [26].
In 5G resilience work, the CMX500 is used as a network emulator for an unmodified 5G DUT [17].
【推論】For a radar-involved A&D system, the Signaling Tester would fit after the communications DUT or radio subsystem is ready to attach to an emulated 5G/NTN network, where its role is to establish the DUT connection and verify RF, mobility, application, NTN, desense, fading/channel, and pre-conformance behavior [1][17][26].
【推論】The Non-signaling Tester would fit earlier or in parallel in R&D/RF verification, where its supported role is non-signaling verification, new-band R&D verification, sensitivity testing, desense testing, and RF measurements [9].
【推論】It should be treated as a communications/network-emulation and RF-verification tool around the radar platform, not as a radar waveform, target-simulation, or radar-performance validation tool, because the supplied passages only support cellular/NTN/private-5G/ISAC-related test roles [1][3][9][10][17][26].
